claim: The ge in geri cannot be built from the 下 card, which teaches only shita, and the back does not say this reading is new, so a learner reading it as shitari thinks they misremembered the kanji card.
evidence: 下痢 back: 'Says: geri'. Lesson 4 下 back: 'Says: shita'. Earlier 下 words: 地下鉄 chikatetsu, 下手 heta; none uses ge.
fix: Add ge to the 下 card's readings, or a note on 下痢 that 下 reads ge here.

claim: The shi in shika cannot be built from the 歯 card, which teaches only ha, and the same chapter's 歯医者 reads haisha, so a learner reads 歯科 as haka and has nothing on the back saying why it is shika.
evidence: 歯科 back: 'Says: shika'. Lesson 7 歯 back: 'Says: ha'. 歯医者 back in this unit: 'Says: haisha'.
fix: Add shi to the 歯 card's readings, or a note on 歯科 that 歯 reads shi here.

claim: The futsuka in futsukayoi cannot be built from the 二 card (ni / futa), and 二日 was never carded on its own, so the back gives a reading the learner cannot connect to the kanji they know without saying it is a whole-word reading.
evidence: 二日酔い back: 'Says: futsukayoi'. Lesson 4 二 back: 'Says: ni / futa'. 日 back: 'ni, nichi, nit-, jitsu / bi, hi, ka'. No 二日 card in the ledger.
fix: Add a note that 二日 reads futsuka (the 2nd, or two days) as a whole word.

claim: The reading kaze leaves 邪 unpronounced, which the 風 and 邪 cards do not prepare for, and the back does not say this is a whole-word reading, so a learner who reads kazeja thinks they got it wrong for a reason they cannot see.
evidence: 風邪 back: 'Says: kaze'. Lesson 3 風 back: 'fū, fu / kaze, kaza'. 邪 back in this unit: 'Says: ja'.
fix: Add a note that 風邪 is read kaze as a whole word, with 邪 silent.

claim: The kano in kanojo cannot be built from the 彼 card, which in this same unit teaches only kare, so a learner reads 彼女 as karejo and the back does not say 彼 has a second reading.
evidence: 彼女 back: 'Says: kanojo'. 彼 back in this unit: 'Answer: He; boyfriend / Says: kare'. 彼氏 back: 'Says: kareshi'.
fix: Add kano to the 彼 card's readings, or a note on 彼女 that 彼 reads kano here.

claim: The romaji carries a tilde that is not on the front, while the English gives no slot marker, so the back reads as if part of the word is missing and does not say what 代 attaches to.
evidence: 代 front: '代'. Back: 'Answer: Charge; fee / Says: ~dai'. Other suffix cards mark the slot in the English, e.g. 行目 'Line number . . .', 週間 'For ... weeks'.
fix: Drop the tilde from the romaji and gloss it '... charge; ... fee' so the slot is marked in the English like the other suffix cards.

claim: 'Physician' reads as a plain synonym of the 医者 'Doctor' the learner already knows, and nothing says 内科 is internal medicine, while the same chapter glosses 眼科 and 歯科 as the field or clinic, so the learner cannot tell what 内 adds or why 科 is sometimes a person and sometimes a department.
evidence: 内科 back: 'Answer: Physician'. Lesson 10 医者 back: 'Answer: Doctor'. Lesson 6 科 back: 'Course; department'. This unit: 眼科 'Ophthalmology (eye clinic)', 歯科 'Dentistry (dental clinic)', 外科 'Surgeon'.
fix: Gloss it 'Internal medicine; physician' so the back names the department the kanji spell.
